newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent firms, gas oil slips before expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent firms, gas oil slips before expiry.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures bounced firmer on Thursday after posting a new 13-month low in late trade on Wednesday.
July Brent was up 15 cents at $17.50 a barrel by 1000 GMT. June gas oil was $1.50 lower at $160.75.
Wednesday's fall in the Brent price to a low of $17.32 came amid market speculation of a slow start to the next six months of the U.N./Iraq oil-for-food deal, brokers said.
The chairman of the U.N. Sanctions Committee said Baghdad was awaiting procedures to be agreed for implementating a new distribution plan before proposing its oil prices.
"There is certainly a cloud over the deal. It's just putting a bearish tone on things, especially with supply data looking strong too," one dealer said.
Brent built on gains in Singapore to move higher in early trade but dealers said the trend might well be reversed later in the session.
"We had a big fall last night and the market is still weak. We are just waiting for the (United) States to come in ," another dealer said.

In the gas oil market, volume was low despite the expiry of the June contract at 1100 GMT. Brokers said the price had fallen back in line with the late drop in Brent after the gas oil close on Wednesday.
Official data showing Singapore's weekly middle distillates at the highest level since at least January 1994 reinforced the bearish tone for gas oil, brokers said.
Trade was expected to pick up just before the expiry and thereafter the market would look to the U.S. for its lead. Though dealers cited good support at $160.00 they said any gains would be fragile.
